title: Proportional Engagement Scheduler for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a new autoscaling policy engine variant — the 'Proportional Engagement Scheduler' — that targets per-tenant committed throughput and observed engagement to deliver predictable latency SLOs while bounding cost and avoiding oscillation on Dedicated fleets.

Context: Current autoscalers focus on single metric thresholds or complex ML predictors. For Dedicated customers with committed throughput, we need a deterministic, auditable policy that: (1) meets per-tenant throughput guarantees under bursty demand, (2) limits unsafe scale-ups during noisy spikes, and (3) provides explicit knobs for cost/latency trade-offs.

Design summary (high level):
- Target metrics: composite throughput target composed of committed_rate (customer contract), short-window observed_qps (1s-30s), and p95/p99 latency headroom. The primary objective is to maintain committed_rate with latency < configured percentile target; secondary objective is cost minimization.
- Algorithm: proportional-integral (PI) controller with adaptive proportional gain. The controller computes desired_capacity = base_committed_capacity + PI(adjustment_from_observed_engagement). Adaptive gain reduces sensitivity when burstiness_detected > threshold (burstiness estimated via coefficient of variation over sliding window).
- Smoothing & actuation: continuous controller output is mapped to discrete instance counts via a quanta-based allocator (GPU slot sizes). We apply a conservative stepper to avoid >2x increase in a single action and a minimum cooldown window per-tenant.
- Safety limits and guardrails: configurable max_scale_rate (instances per minute), min_instance_count floor tied to contract, surge_fence that caps total fleet expansion ratio, global cost cap per-customer, emergency fallback to lighter-weight model variants or routing to hosted pool when safety limits reached.

Why this differs: Emphasizes per-tenant committed throughput and 'engagement' (observed active sessions) rather than only percentile latency or raw QPS. The adaptive PI approach is intentionally simple for auditability while adding burst-aware damping to avoid cascade scaling.
tasks: Spec: finalize config schema for policy (target_metric fields, smoothing_window, percentile_target, max_scale_rate, min_instances, surge_fence)
Proto: implement simulator to validate PI gain schedule against synthetic burst profiles
Runtime: integrate controller into scaling orchestrator with quanta allocator and conservative stepper
Safety: add surge_fence enforcement and global per-customer cost cap checks
Tests: unit tests for controller math, chaos tests for noisy inputs, and e2e on a canary dedicated pool
Docs: README and console UI knobs + recommended defaults for PLG customers
PR: code review and merge, then staged rollout to 'canary-dedicated' followed by 4-week observation
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows <5% SLA violations (latency exceedance) on 95th percentile for defined synthetic workloads while limiting average extra capacity to <15% over committed baseline
Controller enforces max_scale_rate and never issues scale action > configured surge_fence in canary runs
Canary run for 7 days with production-like traffic shows no increase in tail error rates and cost delta within expected bounds
Console exposes policy parameters and live metric view; operators can manually override and rollback within 1 minute
comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after design sync with PM and SRE. Agreed to target a simple, auditable controller rather than opaque ML-driven autoscaler.
2026-03-11 — Marco Liang: Implemented first-pass simulator (see link). Observed instability with naive PI gains on bimodal traffic; added burstiness estimator to reduce P-term when CV>1.2.
2026-03-12 — Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed safety limits. Requested explicit global surge_fence and emergency fallback routing to hosted pool. Also requested observability hooks for every scale action.
2026-03-13 — Design review: Decided on 2x single-action cap and 60s tenant cooldown window. PM requested default knobs for PLG vs. Enterprise tiers. Next: runtime integration spike.
